t.7.73.1: Having heeded the sage's words, Rāma went to the sacred lake frequented by the Apsarases in order to perform the evening twilight worship.
t.7.73.2: There, having touched water and performed the evening twilight worship, Rāma entered the hermitage of the great-souled Kumbhayoni.
t.7.73.3: For his meal Agastya prepared for him fruits and roots of many virtues, as well as herbs and pure vegetables.
t.7.73.4: Having eaten that food, which was like nectar, that best of men, pleased and fully content, spent that night there.
t.7.73.5: At daybreak, rising early and performing his morning rites, the best of the Raghus, subduer of foes, approached the sage in order to take his leave.
t.7.73.6: Having saluted the great seer Kumbhasaṃbhava, Rāma said: "I take leave of you; I shall go. You should grant me permission."
t.7.73.7: I am blessed, I am favoured by the sight of the great-souled one. And I shall come here again to see him, for the purification of my own self.
t.7.73.9: Most wondrous is this speech of yours, O Rāma, auspicious in its every syllable; you alone, O Raghunandana, are the purifier of all the worlds.
t.7.73.8: When Kākutstha had spoken thus, the ascetic rich in austerities, whose eye was dharma, supremely pleased, spoke words of wondrous import.
t.7.73.10: O Rāma, whoever behold you even for a moment are purified; having become dwellers of heaven, they are honoured in heaven by the gods.
t.7.73.11: And those living beings on earth who look upon you with fierce eyes shall be struck down by the rod of Yama and go at once to hell.
t.7.73.12: Go, free from anxiety, along a path that is safe and fearless from every quarter. Rule the kingdom righteously, for you are the refuge of the world.
t.7.73.13: Thus addressed by the sage, the wise king, with joined palms and humbly restrained, respectfully saluted that seer of virtuous conduct.
t.7.73.14: Having saluted the foremost of sages and all those ascetics rich in penance, he calmly mounted that Puṣpaka, adorned with gold.
t.7.73.16: Rāma, at ease, was seen in the gold-adorned Puṣpaka, like the moon standing close to the clouds at the coming of the rainy season.
t.7.73.15: As he set forth, the hosts of sages honored him on every side with blessings, he who shone like the great Indra, just as the immortals honor the thousand-eyed Sahasrākṣa.
t.7.73.17: Then, when midday had arrived, Kākutstha, honored on every side, reached Ayodhyā and descended from the aerial chariot.
t.7.73.18: Then, having dismissed the beautiful Puṣpaka, which travels wherever it wishes, Rāma spoke these words to the doorkeeper stationed within the inner courtyard.
t.7.73.19: Go to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, those two of swift valour, announce my arrival, and summon them to me, for it has been long.
